title: Delhi Street Pani Puri (Golgappe)
pairing: Sweet Tamarind Chutney & Sev
steps: Gently crack top of each crispy puri shell with thumb.
Stuff with boiled diced potatoes and black chickpeas.
Drizzle sweet tamarind dates chutney inside.
Fill shell to brim with chilled spicy mint cumin water and eat whole!

title: Crispy Punjabi Potato Samosa
pairing: Mint Chutney & Masala Chai
steps: Knead stiff dough with flour, ajwain, salt, and oil. Rest for 20 mins.
Saute mashed potatoes with green peas, coriander seeds, and spices.
Roll dough cones, fill with spicy potato filling, and seal edges with water.
Deep fry on low-medium flame until crisp and golden.

title: Mumbai Sev Puri Chaat
pairing: Sweet & Spicy Chutneys
steps: Arrange flat papdi crackers on a wide serving plate.
Top each papdi with diced potatoes and chopped onions.
Spoon mint chutney, tamarind chutney, and spicy garlic chutney.
Generously smother with nylon sev and fresh coriander leaves.

title: South Indian Chicken 65
pairing: Lemon Wedges & Slit Green Chillies
steps: Marinate chicken with red chilli, ginger-garlic paste, yogurt, and cornstarch for 20 mins.
Deep fry chicken pieces until crispy red and cooked through.
Prepare tempering (Tadka) in oil with garlic, slit green chillies, and curry leaves.
Toss fried chicken in the tempering for 1 minute.

title: Lucknowi Galouti Kebab
pairing: Mughlai Paratha & Mint Chutney
steps: Mix minced meat with raw papaya paste and let tenderize for 30 mins.
Blend with fried onion paste, shahi spices, ghee, and roasted besan.
Infuse smoke using hot charcoal and ghee (Dhungar method).
Pan fry round patties in ghee over medium heat until melt-in-mouth soft.

title: Hara Bhara Kebab
pairing: Coriander Chutney
steps: Blend blanched spinach and green peas without adding excess water.
Mix green puree with mashed potato, paneer, chaat masala, and breadcrumbs.
Shape into round patties and press a cashew nut on top of each patty.
Shallow fry on griddle until crisp golden green on both sides.

title: Amritsari Crispy Fish Fry
pairing: Lacha Onion & Lemon Juice
steps: Marinate fish with lemon juice, ginger garlic, ajwain, and Kashmiri chilli.
Coat evenly with besan and rice flour batter.
Deep fry until crispy brown and sprinkle with chaat masala.

title: Butter Chicken
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Marinate chicken with salt and half the ginger-garlic paste.
Cook chicken until lightly browned.
Cook tomato puree with butter and spices until glossy.
Add chicken and a little water; simmer until cooked.
Stir in cream and garam masala; serve hot.

title: Palak Paneer
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Blanch spinach and blend to a smooth puree.
Saute cumin and onion until soft.
Add tomatoes and spices; cook until the oil separates.
Add spinach puree and paneer.
Finish with cream and garam masala.

title: Hyderabadi Biryani
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Marinate chicken with yogurt, spices and herbs.
Parboil basmati rice until about three-quarters cooked.
Layer chicken and rice with fried onion, mint and saffron.
Cover tightly and cook on low heat.
Rest before opening and gently mix.

title: Dal Makhani
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Soak lentils and beans, then pressure-cook until soft.
Saute cumin and ginger-garlic in butter.
Add tomato puree and cook down.
Stir in lentils and simmer slowly.
Add cream and adjust seasoning.

title: Rogan Josh
pairing: Steamed basmati rice or naan
steps: Heat oil and bloom whole spices.
Brown the meat well.
Lower heat and add Kashmiri chili and asafoetida.
Whisk yogurt and add it gradually, stirring continuously.
Add water and simmer covered until the meat is tender and the gravy is rich.
Finish with fennel and ginger powders.

title: Goan Coastal Fish Curry (Xitti)
pairing: Steamed Red Rice / Basmati
steps: Blend coconut, red chillies, coriander seeds, turmeric, and tamarind into smooth paste.
Simmer spicy coconut gravy in a clay pot.
Gently lower fish steaks into bubbling curry; cook 8-10 mins.

title: Royal Malai Kofta Curry
pairing: Butter Naan / Jeera Rice
steps: Mix paneer, potato, and khoya; stuff with cashews/raisins and shape into balls.
Deep fry koftas until golden brown.
Prepare smooth golden gravy with cashews, tomatoes, and aromatic sweet spices.
Place koftas in serving dish and pour hot gravy over top before serving.

title: Chettinad Spicy Pepper Chicken
pairing: Parotta / Steamed Rice
steps: Dry roast black pepper, fennel, cumin, and dry red chillies; grind fresh.
Sauté shallots and curry leaves in gingelly oil.
Add chicken and roasted Chettinad masala powder; roast (Bhunao) until dry and dark.

title: Chole Bhature
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Make a soft bhature dough with flour, yogurt, salt and water; rest it.
Cook onion, tomato and spices into a thick masala.
Add chickpeas and simmer until flavorful.
Roll dough portions and fry until puffed.
Serve bhature with hot chole.

title: Crispy Masala Dosa with Sambhar
pairing: Coconut Chutney & Sambhar
steps: Prepare Potato Masala: Temper mustard seeds, curry leaves, and onions; mix mashed potatoes.
Spread dosa batter thin on hot griddle (Tawa).
Drizzle ghee along edges until golden crisp.
Place potato masala in center and fold into crispy cone.

title: Steamed Soft Fluffy Idli
pairing: Tomato Chutney & Podi Ghee
steps: Grease idli steamer plates lightly with oil.
Pour fermented batter into moulds.
Steam on high heat for 10-12 minutes until fluffy and non-sticky.

title: Tandoori Garlic Butter Naan
pairing: Dal Makhani or Paneer Butter Masala
steps: Knead soft dough with flour, yogurt, pinch of baking soda, and warm water.
Roll teardrop shape, press minced garlic and coriander on top.
Apply water on back side and stick onto piping hot cast iron skillet.
Invert skillet over direct flame until scorched tandoori spots appear; brush with butter.

title: Aromatic Fragrant Jeera Rice
pairing: Dal Tadka or Rajma Masala
steps: Soak basmati rice for 30 minutes; boil until 90% tender and drain.
Heat ghee in pan; sizzle cumin seeds, bay leaf, and cinnamon until fragrant.
Gently fold in boiled rice with fresh coriander leaves.

title: Shahi Hot Gulab Jamun
pairing: Vanilla Ice Cream
steps: Knead soft dough with khoya and maida without overworking.
Shape smooth balls without cracks.
Deep fry on ultra-low heat until dark golden brown.
Soak in warm saffron cardamom sugar syrup for 2 hours.

title: Bengali Spongy Rasgulla
pairing: Chilled Rose Syrup
steps: Curdle milk with lemon juice; knead fresh soft Chenna until completely smooth.
Roll smooth balls.
Boil sugar and water syrup on high heat; drop Chenna balls in boiling syrup.
Cover and boil vigorously for 15 minutes until doubled in size and spongy.

title: Royal Mango Lassi
pairing: Samosa / Kachori
steps: Combine mango pulp, thick chilled curd, sugar, and cardamom in blender.
Blend until thick, creamy, and frothy.
Garnish with pistachios and saffron strands.

title: Kadak Masala Chai
pairing: Biscuits / Paratha
steps: Boil water with crushed fresh ginger, cardamom, and clove.
Add black tea leaves and boil for 2 minutes.
Pour milk, bring to 3 rolling boils, strain, and serve hot.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Marinate chicken in yogurt, ginger-garlic and spices.
Grill or pan-cook chicken until browned.
Saute onions, then add tomato puree and spices.
Add chicken and simmer for 8–10 minutes.
Serve with naan or rice.

title: Rajma Masala
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Saute cumin and onion.
Add tomatoes and powdered spices; cook into a masala.
Add rajma and enough water.
Simmer for 15–20 minutes.
Finish with garam masala and coriander.

title: Aloo Gobi
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Heat oil and crackle cumin.
Add potato and cauliflower with turmeric.
Add tomato and remaining spices.
Cover and cook until tender, stirring occasionally.
Garnish with coriander.

title: Kadai Paneer
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Dry-roast coriander seeds and crush them.
Saute onion and capsicum.
Add tomatoes and spices; cook until thick.
Add paneer and crushed coriander.
Toss for a few minutes and serve.

title: Matar Paneer
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Saute cumin and onion.
Add tomato puree and spices.
Add peas and a splash of water; cook until tender.
Add paneer and simmer briefly.
Finish with garam masala.

title: Aloo Paratha
pairing: Curd, pickle & butter
steps: Knead wheat flour with salt and water into a soft dough.
Mix mashed potatoes with chili, cumin, spices and coriander.
Stuff dough portions with the potato mixture and roll gently.
Cook on a hot tawa with ghee or oil until golden spots appear on both sides.

title: Paneer Tikka
pairing: Mint chutney & onion rings
steps: Whisk hung curd with spices, ginger-garlic, lemon and oil.
Marinate paneer, onion and capsicum for at least 30 minutes.
Thread on skewers.
Grill in a very hot oven, air fryer or tandoor until lightly charred, turning once or twice.

title: Samosa
pairing: Mint chutney & tamarind chutney
steps: Rub flour with oil and salt to a firm dough; rest.
Cook cumin and spices; add potatoes and peas and toss gently.
Roll dough into ovals, cut, shape into cones and fill.
Seal and deep-fry over medium heat until crisp and golden.

title: Kachori
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Make a firm dough and rest it.
Grind soaked dal coarsely and cook with spices.
Fill small dough portions and seal.
Flatten gently and fry until crisp.
Serve with chutney.

title: Pav Bhaji
pairing: Toasted buttered pav, chopped onion & lemon
steps: Boil potatoes, cauliflower and peas; mash them.
Sauté cumin, onion, ginger-garlic and capsicum in butter.
Add tomatoes and spices; cook until soft.
Add mashed vegetables and some water; cook while mashing until smooth.
Finish with lemon and coriander.
Toast pav in butter and serve hot.

title: Vada Pav
pairing: Dry garlic chutney, green chutney & fried chili
steps: Temper mustard, hing, curry leaves, garlic and chili; mix into potatoes with turmeric and coriander.
Shape potato balls.
Whisk besan with turmeric, salt and water into a medium-thick batter.
Dip potato balls in batter and deep-fry until golden.
Split pav and serve with chutneys and the hot vada.

title: Misal Pav
pairing: Pav, farsan, chopped onion & lemon
steps: Cook sprouts and potato until tender.
Temper mustard, cumin and curry leaves; sauté onion, chili and ginger-garlic.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, chili and misal masala.
Add cooked sprouts and enough water to make a spicy usal/rassa; simmer.
Ladle into bowls and top with farsan, onion, tomato and lemon.
Serve immediately with pav.

title: Poha
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Rinse poha and drain.
Temper mustard seeds, curry leaves and peanuts.
Add onion and turmeric.
Fold in poha and warm gently.
Finish with lemon juice.

title: Puran Poli
pairing: Warm milk or ghee
steps: Cook chana dal until just tender, drain well and mash.
Cook dal with jaggery, ghee and spices until the mixture thickens into a soft filling; cool.
Make a soft dough from flours, oil/ghee, salt and water; rest well.
Stuff dough with puran, seal and roll gently.
Cook on a hot tawa with ghee on both sides.

title: Dhokla
pairing: Green chutney & sweet tamarind chutney
steps: Whisk besan, yogurt, water, ginger-chili, turmeric, sugar and salt into a smooth batter.
Just before steaming, mix in lemon juice and fruit salt.
Pour into a greased thali and steam until springy.
Temper oil with mustard, sesame, curry leaves and green chili; pour over dhokla.

title: Thepla
pairing: Yogurt, pickle & chai
steps: Combine flour, methi, besan, spices, yogurt and oil.
Knead with water into a soft dough and rest 15 minutes.
Divide and roll thin like a paratha.
Cook on a hot tawa with a little oil until both sides are browned and cooked through.

title: Undhiyu
pairing: Puri & shrikhand
steps: Mix grated coconut, peanuts, sesame, spices and herbs into a stuffing.
Make small slits in the eggplants, potatoes and bananas and stuff them.
Shape small methi muthia from fenugreek, besan, spices and a little oil; steam or shallow-fry.
Layer hard vegetables, papdi, stuffed vegetables, muthia and spice mixture in a heavy pot.
Add a splash of water and oil, cover tightly and cook on low until tender.

title: Dal Baati Churma
pairing: Ghee, garlic chutney & buttermilk

ingredients.name: coarse wheat flour or atta for churma

steps: Make sturdy baati dough with wheat flour, semolina, ghee, ajwain and salt.
Bake baatis until browned and cooked through.
Cook dal with turmeric and salt, then temper with ghee and spices.
For churma, crumble baked baati, mix with ghee, sugar/jaggery, cardamom and nuts.
Soak baati pieces in ghee and serve with dal and churma.

title: Gatte Ki Sabzi
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Mix besan with spices and a little oil; shape into logs.
Boil logs, cool and slice.
Whisk yogurt with spices.
Cook yogurt gravy gently and add gatte.
Simmer briefly and serve.

title: Laal Maas
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Soak chillies and blend into a paste.
Brown onions and mutton in oil.
Add ginger-garlic, chilli paste and yogurt gradually.
Add water and cook until mutton is tender.
Adjust seasoning and serve.

title: Ker Sangri
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Soak ker and sangri, then rinse well.
Boil until tender and drain.
Temper cumin in oil.
Add spices, vegetables and yogurt.
Cook until dry and aromatic.

title: Dal Dhokli
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Cook dal until soft and whisk smooth.
Make a dough, roll it thin and cut diamonds.
Bring dal to a simmer with spices and peanuts.
Drop dough pieces in and cook until tender.
Balance with jaggery and lemon.

title: Idli
pairing: Sambar & coconut chutney
steps: Soak rice and urad dal separately for 4–6 hours.
Grind urad dal fluffy and rice slightly grainy; combine with salt.
Ferment the batter overnight in a warm place.
Grease idli molds, fill and steam for 10–12 minutes.
Rest 2 minutes before unmolding.

title: Masala Dosa
pairing: Sambar, coconut chutney & potato masala
steps: Soak rice, urad dal and fenugreek separately for several hours.
Grind with water to a smooth, moderately thick batter and ferment until airy.
Prepare potato masala by tempering mustard, cumin and curry leaves, then sautéing onion, chili and turmeric before adding potatoes.
Heat a seasoned tawa, spread batter very thin into a circle and drizzle oil.
Place potato masala in the center, fold and serve crisp.

title: Medu Vada
pairing: Sambar & coconut chutney
steps: Soak urad dal 4–5 hours and drain very well.
Grind with minimal water to a thick, fluffy batter.
Fold in pepper, chili, ginger, curry leaves, coriander and salt.
Wet your hands, shape ring-shaped vadas and slide into medium-hot oil.
Fry until crisp and golden.

title: Sambar
pairing: Idli, dosa, vada or rice
steps: Cook toor dal until soft and whisk smooth.
Cook vegetables with tomato, turmeric and water until tender.
Add tamarind, sambar powder and jaggery; simmer.
Stir in cooked dal and adjust consistency.
Temper mustard, cumin, curry leaves, dry chilies and hing in oil; add to the sambar.

title: Rasam
pairing: Steamed rice & papad
steps: Crush or puree tomatoes and simmer with tamarind, water and turmeric.
Add rasam powder, cumin, pepper and salt; heat until fragrant and just before a hard boil.
Temper mustard, cumin, curry leaves, red chili and hing in ghee/oil.
Pour tempering over rasam and garnish with coriander.

title: Lemon Rice
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Cool cooked rice slightly.
Temper mustard, peanuts, chillies and curry leaves.
Add turmeric.
Fold in rice and lemon juice.
Rest for a few minutes before serving.

title: Tamarind Rice
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Cook tamarind with spices into a thick paste.
Temper mustard, peanuts and curry leaves.
Mix paste into rice gradually.
Add roasted sesame.
Rest before serving.

title: Coconut Rice
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Temper mustard, peanuts, chillies and curry leaves.
Add coconut and cook briefly.
Fold in rice and salt.
Warm gently without drying it.
Serve with a vegetable curry.

title: Pongal
pairing: Coconut chutney & sambar
steps: Dry-roast moong dal lightly.
Pressure-cook rice and dal together with water and salt until soft.
Fry cumin, pepper, ginger, cashews, curry leaves and hing in ghee.
Mix the tempering into the cooked pongal and serve hot.

title: Uttapam
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Heat a tawa and pour a thick ladle of batter.
Top with chopped vegetables.
Drizzle oil around the edges.
Cook both sides until golden.
Serve with chutney.

title: Appam
pairing: Vegetable stew or coconut milk
steps: Soak raw rice 4–5 hours.
Blend rice with cooked rice and coconut into a smooth batter.
Mix yeast, sugar and warm water; stir into batter and ferment until slightly bubbly.
Adjust with coconut milk and salt to a pourable consistency.
Swirl a ladleful in a hot appam pan, cover and cook until lacy at the edges and soft in the center.

title: Kerala Vegetable Stew
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Saute ginger and whole spices in coconut oil.
Add vegetables and thin coconut milk.
Cover and cook until tender.
Add thick coconut milk and warm gently.
Finish with curry leaves.

title: Avial
pairing: Steamed rice
steps: Cook firm vegetables with turmeric, salt and a little water, adding softer vegetables later.
Grind coconut, green chili and cumin to a coarse paste.
Fold the coconut paste into the vegetables and simmer briefly.
Lower heat, mix in yogurt and never allow it to boil hard.
Finish with coconut oil and curry leaves.

title: Kerala Fish Curry
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Rub fish lightly with turmeric and salt.
Cook onion and spices in coconut oil.
Add tamarind and coconut milk.
Slide in fish and simmer gently until cooked.
Finish with curry leaves.

title: Malabar Parotta
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Make a soft, elastic dough and rest it well.
Stretch and fold dough with oil into layers.
Coil each portion and rest again.
Flatten gently and cook on a hot tawa.
Fluff by clapping the cooked parotta between your hands.

title: Hyderabadi Veg Biryani
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Marinate vegetables with yogurt and spices.
Parboil rice.
Layer vegetables, rice, herbs and saffron.
Seal and cook on low heat.
Rest, fluff and serve.

title: Mirchi ka Salan
pairing: Hyderabadi biryani & plain rice
steps: Slit chilies lengthwise and shallow-fry until lightly blistered; set aside.
Roast peanuts, sesame and coconut; grind with onion, ginger and garlic.
Temper mustard, nigella, cumin and curry leaves in oil.
Add the ground paste and powdered spices; cook until fragrant.
Add tamarind and water, then simmer until the gravy thickens.
Add the chilies and cook for a few minutes more.

title: Bagara Rice
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Saute whole spices and sliced onion.
Add rinsed rice and stir briefly.
Add water and salt.
Cook covered until rice is tender.
Rest and garnish with coriander.

title: Chicken Chettinad
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Roast coconut and whole spices; grind coarsely.
Brown onion and add tomatoes.
Add spice paste and chicken.
Add water and simmer until tender.
Finish with curry leaves.

title: Chettinad Vegetable Curry
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Roast coconut and spices and grind.
Saute onion and tomatoes.
Add masala and cook until aromatic.
Add vegetables and water.
Simmer until tender.

title: Pesarattu
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Soak green gram for several hours.
Blend with ginger, chilli, cumin and water.
Spread thinly on a hot tawa.
Top with onion and cook until crisp.
Fold and serve.

title: Andhra Tomato Pappu
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Cook dal with tomatoes, chilli and turmeric.
Mash lightly.
Temper mustard, cumin and curry leaves in ghee.
Stir tempering into dal.
Serve with rice.

title: Goan Fish Curry
pairing: Steamed rice & fried fish or papad
steps: Marinate fish with lemon, turmeric and salt.
Blend coconut, chilies, coriander, cumin, pepper, ginger, garlic, tamarind and onion into a smooth paste.
Fry the paste in oil until fragrant.
Add thin coconut milk and simmer briefly.
Add fish and cook gently until just done.
Finish with thick coconut milk without boiling hard.

title: Goan Vegetable Xacuti
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Roast coconut and whole spices.
Grind with water into a paste.
Saute onion and add paste.
Add vegetables and simmer until tender.
Adjust seasoning and serve.

title: Maharashtrian Amti Dal
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Cook dal until soft.
Whisk in turmeric and water.
Add goda masala, tamarind and jaggery.
Temper mustard and curry leaves in ghee.
Simmer briefly and serve.

title: Thalipeeth
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Mix flour with onion, spices and water into a soft dough.
Pat a portion thinly onto a greased pan.
Make small holes and drizzle oil.
Cook both sides until crisp.
Serve with yogurt.

title: Bengali Shorshe Ilish
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Rub fish with turmeric and salt.
Warm mustard oil and add mustard paste with water.
Place fish pieces and green chillies into the sauce.
Cover and cook gently until fish is done.
Serve with steamed rice.

title: Bengali Aloo Posto
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Soak and grind poppy seeds with water.
Heat mustard oil and temper nigella seeds.
Add potatoes and cook lightly.
Add poppy paste and green chilli.
Cover and cook until potatoes are tender.

title: Cholar Dal
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Cook chana dal until tender but intact.
Fry coconut pieces in ghee.
Temper cumin and bay leaf.
Add ginger and dal with a little water.
Balance with a little sugar and salt.

title: Macher Jhol
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Rub fish and potatoes with turmeric and salt.
Lightly pan-sear fish and potatoes.
Cook cumin, tomato and spices in oil.
Add water and potatoes.
Return fish and simmer gently.

title: Kosha Mangsho
pairing: Luchi or steamed rice
steps: Marinate mutton with yogurt, ginger-garlic and half the spices.
Slowly caramelize onions in mustard oil until deep brown.
Add whole spices, tomatoes and the remaining spices.
Add marinated mutton and bhuno on medium heat until oil releases and the meat is coated in dark masala.
Add warm water, cover and cook slowly until the meat is tender and the gravy is thick.

title: Momos
pairing: Chili-garlic chutney
steps: Knead a firm dough with flour, salt and water; rest.
Mix filling ingredients thoroughly.
Roll small wrappers, place filling in the center and pleat into momos.
Steam in a greased steamer for 10–12 minutes until cooked.

title: Thukpa
pairing: Chili sauce & fresh herbs
steps: Sauté onion, ginger, garlic and chili.
Add chicken and cook until opaque.
Add stock, carrot, cabbage and tomato; simmer until vegetables are tender.
Add noodles and soy sauce; cook until noodles are done.
Finish with pepper, spring onion and coriander.

title: Kashmiri Rajma
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Saute cumin and tomato.
Add Kashmiri spices and cook briefly.
Add rajma and water.
Simmer until the gravy thickens.
Adjust salt and serve with rice.

title: Dum Aloo Kashmiri
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Boil and prick potatoes, then lightly fry them.
Whisk yogurt with spices.
Cook the yogurt mixture gently with water.
Add potatoes and simmer covered.
Finish when the gravy coats the potatoes.

title: Matar Kulcha
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Cook peas with tomato, onion and spices.
Make a soft kulcha dough with flour and yogurt.
Rest, roll and cook kulcha on a hot tawa.
Top with coriander.
Serve with matar.

title: Pani Puri
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Blend mint and coriander with water.
Mix tamarind, cumin and chaat masala into the pani.
Prepare potato-chickpea filling.
Crack each puri and fill.
Add pani just before eating.

title: Bhel Puri
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Mix puffed rice with vegetables.
Add both chutneys.
Season with chaat masala.
Toss quickly to keep it crisp.
Top with sev and coriander.

title: Dahi Puri
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Fill puris with potato.
Add chilled yogurt and both chutneys.
Sprinkle chaat masala.
Top with sev and coriander.
Serve immediately.

title: Gulab Jamun
pairing: Vanilla ice cream or rabri
steps: Knead khoya, maida, soda and ghee into a smooth soft dough, adding milk sparingly.
Shape small crack-free balls.
Make a light sugar syrup with water, sugar, cardamom and rose water.
Fry balls over medium-low heat until evenly deep golden.
Soak warm jamuns in warm syrup for at least 1 hour.

title: Jalebi
pairing: Rabri & milk
steps: Whisk maida, besan, turmeric and baking powder with water into a smooth batter.
Rest the batter briefly.
Make a one-string sugar syrup with water and saffron.
Pipe spirals into hot oil or ghee and fry crisp.
Dip briefly in warm syrup and serve immediately.

title: Rasgulla
pairing: Chilled or at room temperature
steps: Boil milk and curdle with lemon juice.
Strain, rinse and press the chhena until just moist.
Knead until smooth, sprinkle in semolina and shape small crack-free balls.
Boil sugar and water in a wide pot.
Add the balls, cover and simmer until they puff and become spongy.
Flavor the syrup with cardamom and rose/kewra water.

title: Sandesh
pairing: Light Bengali tea
steps: Bring milk to a boil, lower heat and add lemon juice until the curds separate.
Strain through cloth and rinse lightly; press out excess whey to make fresh chhena.
Knead chhena until smooth, then cook with sugar in a nonstick pan on low heat until the mixture comes together.
Cool slightly, add cardamom, shape into small sandesh and garnish with nuts.

title: Kheer
pairing: Saffron, pistachio & almonds
steps: Rinse rice and soak 20 minutes.
Bring milk to a simmer and add rice.
Cook slowly, stirring often, until the rice breaks down and the milk thickens.
Add sugar, saffron and cardamom.
Fold in nuts and raisins and chill or serve warm.

title: Gajar Ka Halwa
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Grate carrots.
Cook carrots with milk until most liquid evaporates.
Add sugar and ghee.
Cook until glossy and thick.
Finish with cardamom and nuts.

title: Shrikhand
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Hang yogurt in a cloth until thick.
Whisk with powdered sugar.
Add cardamom and saffron.
Chill well.
Top with pistachios.

title: Mango Lassi
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Blend mango, yogurt and milk.
Sweeten to taste.
Add cardamom.
Chill or blend with a few ice cubes.
Serve cold.

title: Masala Chai
pairing: Biscuits or savory snacks
steps: Crush ginger and cardamom lightly.
Boil water with cinnamon, cloves, cardamom and ginger for a few minutes.
Add tea and simmer briefly.
Add milk and sugar and bring to a strong boil.
Strain and serve hot.

title: Filter Coffee
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Brew strong coffee decoction.
Heat milk and sweeten to taste.
Combine coffee and milk.
Pour between two cups for a frothy top.
Serve hot.

title: Lassi
pairing: Roasted cumin or saffron
steps: Whisk or blend yogurt until smooth.
Add cold water/milk, sugar and cardamom.
Blend until frothy and pour over ice.
Sprinkle roasted cumin for a traditional savory-style finish or omit for sweet lassi.

title: Shahi Paneer
pairing: Naan or fragrant basmati rice
steps: Cook onion, nuts, seeds, ginger and garlic in water until tender; blend smooth.
Heat ghee and gently cook the nut-onion paste with powdered spices.
Lower heat and stir in yogurt gradually to prevent splitting.
Add paneer, cardamom and saffron; simmer briefly.
Finish with cream and sugar; adjust salt.

title: Malai Kofta
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Mash paneer and potato, mix with cornflour and shape into balls.
Fry koftas until golden.
Blend cooked tomato and cashew into a smooth paste.
Cook the paste with spices and cream.
Add koftas just before serving.

title: Bhindi Masala
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Wash and dry okra thoroughly, then slice.
Saute okra until lightly cooked and set aside.
Cook cumin, onion and tomato with spices.
Return okra to the pan.
Cook uncovered until tender.

title: Baingan Bharta
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Roast eggplant until the skin is charred and the inside is soft.
Peel and mash the eggplant.
Saute cumin, onion, chilli and tomato.
Add mashed eggplant and cook together.
Finish with coriander.

title: Kadhi Pakora
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Whisk yogurt, besan, turmeric and water.
Cook the kadhi gently until thick and smooth.
Make a seasoned besan batter and fry small pakoras.
Add pakoras to the kadhi.
Temper cumin and add before serving.

title: Navratan Korma
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Cook vegetables until just tender.
Blend cashews with a little water.
Cook cashew paste in ghee with spices.
Add yogurt and cream gently.
Fold in vegetables, raisins and a few cashews.

title: Methi Matar Malai
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Blanch methi briefly and chop.
Blend onion and cashews into a paste.
Cook cumin and paste until fragrant.
Add peas, methi and a little water.
Finish with cream and garam masala.

title: Litti Chokha
pairing: Tomato chokha, eggplant chokha & ghee
steps: Make a firm wheat dough with salt, ghee and water.
Mix sattu with spices, herbs, lemon juice, mustard oil and a little water to form a crumbly stuffing.
Stuff dough balls with sattu and seal.
Bake or charcoal-roast litti until browned and cooked through; crack slightly and dip in ghee.
Roast eggplant and tomatoes, peel and mash with onion, chili, garlic, coriander, mustard oil and salt for chokha.

title: Sattu Paratha
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Make a soft wheat dough.
Mix sattu with onion, chilli, ajwain, coriander and water.
Stuff dough balls and roll gently.
Cook on a hot tawa with oil.
Serve with yogurt or pickle.

title: Chana Ghugni
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Saute cumin and onion.
Add tomato and spices.
Add cooked peas and a little water.
Simmer until thick.
Finish with lemon and coriander.

title: Sarson Ka Saag
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Wash and chop the greens.
Cook greens with ginger and a little water until soft.
Blend or mash to the desired texture.
Return to heat and stir in maize flour.
Finish with ghee and serve with roti.

title: Makki di Roti
pairing: Sarson da Saag & white butter
steps: Mix maize flour, ajwain and salt.
Add hot water gradually and knead into a soft dough while warm.
Divide into balls and pat each between plastic sheets or damp hands into a thick roti.
Cook on a hot tawa until browned on both sides, applying ghee.

title: Tandoori Chicken
pairing: Mint-coriander chutney & onion salad
steps: Make deep slashes in the chicken.
Marinate with lemon, ginger-garlic, salt and spices; rest 30 minutes.
Coat with yogurt marinade and refrigerate for several hours or overnight.
Roast in a very hot oven, grill or tandoor, turning until charred and fully cooked.
Rest briefly before serving.

title: Fish Amritsari
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Mix besan, spices, lemon and water into a thick batter.
Coat fish pieces evenly.
Fry or shallow-fry until crisp and cooked through.
Drain excess oil.
Serve with lemon.

title: Aloo Tikki
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Mash potatoes with spices and cornflour.
Shape into flat patties.
Pan-fry with a little oil until crisp on both sides.
Sprinkle with chaat masala.
Serve with chutney.

title: Raj Kachori
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Fill each shell with chickpeas.
Add yogurt and chutneys.
Sprinkle chaat masala.
Top with sev and coriander.
Serve immediately.

title: Mysore Masala Dosa
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Blend roasted gram, chilli and garlic into a red chutney.
Make a spiced potato filling.
Spread dosa batter thinly.
Apply red chutney and add potato filling.
Fold when crisp.

title: Bisi Bele Bath
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Cook rice and dal until soft.
Cook vegetables separately until tender.
Combine with spice powder and tamarind.
Simmer until thick and creamy.
Finish with ghee and cashews.

title: Mangalore Buns
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Mash bananas with yogurt and sugar.
Mix in flour, cumin, salt and baking soda.
Rest the dough for several hours.
Roll small discs and fry gently until puffed.
Serve with chutney or yogurt.

title: Mutton Rogan Josh
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Brown mutton lightly with whole spices.
Add yogurt gradually while stirring.
Add Kashmiri chilli and fennel.
Add water, cover and cook slowly until tender.
Adjust seasoning before serving.

title: Kashmiri Pulao
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Saute whole spices and nuts in ghee.
Add rinsed rice and stir briefly.
Add water and salt; cook covered.
Fold in fruit and raisins.
Rest before serving.

title: Methi Thepla
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Mix flour, methi, yogurt and spices into a soft dough.
Rest briefly.
Roll thin circles.
Cook on a hot tawa with oil.
Serve with yogurt or pickle.

title: Khaman
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Whisk besan with water, lemon, sugar and salt.
Fold in fruit salt just before steaming.
Steam until fluffy.
Temper mustard, curry leaves and chilli.
Pour tempering over and cut.

title: Kolkata Chicken Biryani
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Marinate chicken with yogurt and spices.
Parboil rice and separately cook potatoes until nearly tender.
Layer chicken, potato, rice and fried onion.
Add a little rose water and ghee.
Cook covered on low heat until done.

title: Mughlai Paratha
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Make and rest a soft flour dough.
Whisk eggs with onion, chilli and coriander.
Roll dough thin and place on a hot pan.
Add egg mixture, fold the edges and cook with oil.
Turn until golden and the filling is set.

title: Pakhala Bhata
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Cool cooked rice completely.
Mix with water and yogurt and rest chilled.
Temper mustard and curry leaves.
Add tempering and chilli.
Serve cold with vegetables or fried sides.

title: Dalma
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Cook dal and vegetables together until tender.
Dry-roast cumin and coriander and crush.
Stir spices into the cooked dal.
Temper chilli and spices in ghee.
Serve with rice.

title: Sikkimese Vegetable Thukpa
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Saute ginger and vegetables.
Add stock and simmer.
Add noodles and cook until tender.
Adjust salt.
Finish with spring onion and coriander.

title: Paneer Bhurji
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Crumble paneer.
Saute cumin, onion and capsicum.
Add tomato and spices.
Fold in paneer and cook for a few minutes.
Serve with roti or toast.

title: Jeera Rice
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Rinse rice well.
Heat ghee and crackle cumin with whole spices.
Add rice and stir briefly.
Add water and salt; cook covered.
Rest and fluff gently.

title: Vegetable Pulao
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Saute whole spices and onion in ghee.
Add vegetables and rice.
Add water and salt.
Cover and cook until rice is tender.
Rest before serving.

title: Aamras
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Peel and chop mangoes.
Blend until smooth.
Adjust sweetness and consistency.
Add cardamom.
Chill and serve.

title: Modak
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Cook coconut and jaggery until thick; add cardamom.
Make a soft rice-flour dough with hot water.
Shape small cups, fill and pleat closed.
Steam until the outer shell is cooked.
Brush lightly with ghee.

title: Payasam
pairing: Fresh coriander, lemon and a traditional Indian side
steps: Cook rice slowly in milk.
Add sugar and continue until creamy.
Fry cashews and raisins in ghee.
Add cardamom.
Stir in the fried nuts and serve warm or chilled.

title: Rajma Chawal
pairing: Plain yogurt & onion rings
steps: Soak rajma overnight; rinse well.
Pressure-cook rajma with water until completely tender.
Cook onion, ginger, garlic and green chili in butter or oil.
Add tomatoes and spices; cook until the masala thickens.
Stir in rajma and simmer until creamy.
Cook basmati rice separately and serve hot with rajma.

title: Sarson da Saag
pairing: Makki di Roti & white butter
steps: Wash and chop all greens and vegetables.
Pressure-cook the greens, radish, onion, tomatoes, ginger, garlic and chilies with water until tender.
Cool slightly, add maize flour and blend to a coarse or smooth texture.
Simmer again until thick and creamy.
Temper with ghee or oil and finely chopped onion; serve hot.
sourceNote: Ingredient structure follows the traditional Punjabi formulation described by Veg Recipes of India, including mustard greens, bathua, spinach, radish, fenugreek and maize flour.

title: Amritsari Kulcha
pairing: Chole & onion pickle
steps: Combine maida, yogurt, oil, sugar, salt and leavening agents; knead to a soft dough and rest.
Mix the potato filling with coriander, cumin, amchur, chili and salt.
Stuff dough balls and roll into kulchas.
Cook in a very hot tandoor or heavy skillet until blistered and browned.
Brush generously with butter or ghee.

title: Nihari
pairing: Khameeri roti & lemon

ingredients.name: wheat flour or atta for slurry

steps: Sear meat in hot oil with whole spices.
Add ginger-garlic and powdered spices; cook briefly.
Cover with water and slow-cook until the meat is very tender.
Mix flour with water and whisk into the broth for a glossy, lightly thickened gravy.
Simmer 10 minutes, finish with lemon, ginger and coriander.

title: Pyaaz Kachori
pairing: Imli chutney & chai
steps: Make a stiff maida dough with oil, salt and water; rest.
Cook onions with spices and besan until the filling is dry and aromatic.
Stuff dough portions with the onion mixture and seal.
Deep-fry on medium-low heat until crisp and evenly browned.

title: Khandvi
pairing: Coconut, coriander & tempered mustard
steps: Whisk besan, yogurt, water and seasonings until lump-free.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring continuously, until the batter becomes thick and spreadable.
Spread immediately into thin layers on steel plates or the back of trays.
Cool briefly, cut into strips and roll tightly.
Temper mustard, sesame and curry leaves in oil; pour over the rolls.

title: Sabudana Khichdi
pairing: Plain yogurt & lemon wedges
steps: Rinse sabudana until the water runs mostly clear and soak until the pearls press soft between your fingers.
Mix with crushed roasted peanuts, salt and sugar.
Temper cumin and green chili in ghee; add potatoes.
Add sabudana mixture and cook briefly until the pearls turn translucent, not mushy.
Finish with lemon and coriander.

title: Vindaloo
pairing: Steamed rice, pao or sannas
steps: Blend vinegar, chilies, cumin, pepper, cloves, cinnamon, ginger, garlic and turmeric into a marinade.
Marinate pork for several hours or overnight.
Brown onions in oil.
Add pork and the marinade; cook until browned.
Add water and simmer covered until the meat is very tender and the sauce is glossy.
Balance with sugar and salt.

title: Bebinca
pairing: Warm or chilled, with vanilla ice cream
steps: Whisk yolks and sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Mix in coconut milk, flour, salt and spices to make a smooth batter.
Grease a baking pan with ghee.
Pour a very thin layer of batter, bake until set, brush with ghee, then repeat layer by layer until all batter is used.
Cool fully before slicing.

title: Puttu
pairing: Kadala curry & banana
steps: Sprinkle salted water over puttu flour little by little and rub to a damp, crumbly texture.
Layer coconut and moistened flour in the puttu maker.
Steam until cooked and aromatic.
Serve hot with kadala curry or ripe banana.

title: Kerala Parotta
pairing: Vegetable kurma or Kerala chicken curry
steps: Make a soft, slightly sticky maida dough with sugar, salt, oil and water.
Knead thoroughly and rest, then divide into balls.
Stretch or roll each ball into a very thin sheet, brush with oil and pleat/spiral into a coil.
Flatten gently and cook on a hot tawa with oil.
Clap or fluff the cooked parotta between your hands to separate layers.

title: Thoran
pairing: Steamed rice & dal
steps: Heat coconut oil and temper mustard, cumin and curry leaves.
Add green chili, the vegetable and turmeric.
Cook covered until just tender, keeping some bite.
Mix in grated coconut and cook 1–2 minutes more.

title: Chettinad Chicken
pairing: Parotta, dosa or steamed rice
steps: Dry-roast whole spices, pepper, coriander seeds and coconut; cool and grind.
Sauté onion and ginger-garlic in oil.
Add tomatoes and ground spice paste; cook until aromatic and oil separates.
Add chicken, turmeric and chili; stir-fry briefly.
Add water, cover and simmer until the chicken is tender.

title: Haleem
pairing: Naan, lemon, ginger & fried onions
steps: Wash and soak grains and dals for several hours.
Cook the meat with spices until tender.
Cook soaked grains and dals separately until completely soft.
Blend or mash the grain-dal mixture until porridge-like.
Shred the meat and stir it into the grain mixture.
Cook together on low heat with ghee until thick and glossy.
Finish with lemon, fried onions and ginger.

title: Kolkata Biryani
pairing: Raita & salad
steps: Marinate chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic, chili, turmeric, cumin and garam masala.
Parboil potatoes and rice separately; keep rice about 70% cooked.
Layer chicken, potatoes, rice and whole spices in a heavy pot.
Add fried onions, saffron, rose/kewra water and ghee.
Place whole boiled eggs on top, seal and cook on low heat until done.

title: Shorshe Ilish
pairing: Steamed rice
steps: Soak mustard seeds briefly, then grind with green chili and a pinch of salt into a smooth paste.
Coat hilsa with turmeric and salt.
Heat mustard oil until it just begins to smoke, then temper with kalonji.
Add mustard paste and water; simmer gently.
Slide in hilsa pieces and cook without turning too much, spooning sauce over the fish.

title: Luchi
pairing: Alur dom or cholar dal

ingredients.name: oil or ghee for deep frying

steps: Rub ghee/oil and salt into maida.
Knead with water into a soft, smooth dough and rest 20 minutes.
Divide, roll small discs and keep them covered.
Deep-fry one at a time in hot oil, pressing gently so they puff.

title: Ghugni
pairing: Luchi, puffed rice or bread
steps: Soak yellow peas overnight and cook until tender.
Temper cumin in mustard oil; sauté onion, ginger and chili.
Add potato and powdered spices; cook briefly.
Add peas, water and tamarind; simmer until the gravy coats the peas.
Finish with coriander.

title: Mishti Doi
pairing: Bengali sweets

ingredients.name: date-palm jaggery (nolen gur) or dark jaggery

steps: Reduce full-fat milk over low heat until noticeably thickened.
Melt jaggery separately with a spoonful of hot milk if needed.
Cool milk until warm, not hot; stir in jaggery and cardamom.
Whisk in yogurt culture and pour into earthen pots or bowls.
Let set undisturbed in a warm place for 6–10 hours, then chill.

title: Dal Bafla
pairing: Dal, ghee & chutney
steps: Knead wheat flour, semolina, ghee, ajwain and salt with water; make sturdy balls.
Boil or bake the balls until cooked through and lightly browned.
Cook dal with turmeric and salt until soft.
Prepare a tempering with ghee, cumin, onion, tomato, chili and spices.
Break bafla into pieces, drizzle with ghee and serve with the dal.

title: Poha Jalebi
pairing: Tea & sev
steps: Rinse poha briefly and drain.
Temper mustard, curry leaves and peanuts; sauté onion, potato and chili.
Add turmeric and poha; toss until hot and fluffy.
Finish with lemon and coriander.
Mix maida, besan and baking powder with water to a smooth batter; pipe spirals into hot oil.
Soak fried jalebis briefly in one-string sugar syrup flavored with saffron.

title: Bhutte ka Kees
pairing: Tea or breakfast

ingredients.name: fresh corn, kernels grated or coarsely crushed

steps: Heat ghee and temper cumin, hing, chili and ginger.
Add grated corn and turmeric; cook until the raw smell disappears.
Add milk and cook while stirring until the corn is tender and creamy.
Finish with coconut, coriander and salt.

title: Mysore Pak
pairing: South Indian coffee
steps: Roast besan lightly to remove its raw aroma.
Make a one-string sugar syrup with water and sugar.
Add besan gradually while stirring.
Add hot ghee in batches and keep stirring until the mixture turns glossy and begins to leave the pan.
Spread into a greased tray, cool and cut.

title: Dharwad Peda
pairing: Filter coffee
steps: Reduce milk slowly until thick, then mix in khoya.
Cook the milk-khoya mixture with sugar until deeply caramelized and crumbly.
Add ghee and cardamom.
Cool slightly, portion and shape into small rough-edged pedas.

title: Chhena Poda
pairing: Warm or room temperature
steps: Knead fresh chhena until smooth.
Mix in sugar, semolina, cardamom, nuts and raisins.
Line a pan with ghee and pour in the mixture.
Bake until the top is deeply caramelized and the center is set.
Cool before slicing.

title: Thekua
pairing: Tea or festival offering
steps: Dissolve jaggery in warm water and cool slightly.
Rub ghee into flour, then add coconut and fennel.
Add jaggery water little by little to make a firm dough.
Shape embossed discs.
Deep-fry on medium heat until deep golden and crisp.

title: Khar
pairing: Steamed rice & dal
steps: Cook the raw papaya in water until tender.
Temper mustard seeds or panch phoron in mustard oil.
Add ginger and chili.
Stir in cooked dal and khar water; simmer gently and adjust salt.
sourceNote: Assamese khar has many family and ingredient variations; this app uses a common raw-papaya and pulse version.

title: Masor Tenga
pairing: Steamed rice

ingredients.name: rohu or other firm freshwater fish

steps: Rub fish with turmeric and salt; pan-fry lightly in mustard oil and set aside.
Temper fenugreek seeds in the oil.
Add tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add water and simmer to make a light sour broth.
Return fish and finish with lemon juice.

title: Jadoh
pairing: Fresh herbs & chili
steps: Brown the pork in oil.
Add onion, ginger, garlic and chili and cook until fragrant.
Stir in washed red rice, turmeric, pepper and salt.
Add water and cook covered until the rice is tender and pork is cooked through.
sourceNote: Jadoh varies across Meghalaya households; this version uses the familiar pork-and-rice base.

title: Ghevar
pairing: Rabri & saffron
steps: Whisk ghee and cold water until emulsified; add milk and flour to make a very thin batter.
Heat ghee/oil in a deep vessel with a central opening or use a deep pan.
Pour a small amount of batter from a height into the hot fat to form a lacy disc; repeat until the desired thickness is achieved.
Fry until crisp and golden, then drain.
Dip briefly in sugar syrup and serve with rabri.

title: Rasmalai
pairing: Chilled
steps: Make soft chhena from milk and lemon juice; knead smooth and shape discs.
Reduce the second batch of milk until creamy; add sugar, cardamom and saffron.
Poach chhena discs gently in light sugar water until they expand.
Squeeze gently and transfer to the thickened milk.
Chill and garnish with nuts.

title: Kulfi
pairing: Pistachios & saffron
steps: Simmer milk until reduced.
Whisk rice flour with 3 tbsp milk and add it to the hot milk.
Cook until slightly thickened.
Add khoya, sugar, cardamom and saffron; stir until dissolved.
Cool, add nuts, pour into molds and freeze until firm.

title: Falooda
pairing: Serve chilled
steps: Soak basil seeds in water until swollen.
Boil falooda sev and chill.
Layer rose syrup, basil seeds, sev and sweetened cold milk in tall glasses.
Top with ice cream and nuts.

title: Thandai
pairing: Chilled during Holi
steps: Soak nuts, poppy and melon seeds for 3–4 hours.
Grind with rose petals, fennel, pepper, cardamom and saffron into a smooth paste.
Mix with a little milk and strain if desired.
Combine with the remaining chilled milk and sugar; chill thoroughly before serving.
